answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when its work is proven false, so a Sybil attacker must pay per copy instead of cloning for free. Like a grove where every tree needs its own roots, water, and sunlight, each agent must fund its own stake, pass a dawn check of prior useful work, and keep a regular pulse of verifiable tasks; identities that go silent or cheat lose the bond, making mass fakery expensive and easy to prune.
